text:
Kent Johnson finally has the role that the fifth overall pick in 2021 was supposed to get. He plays 18:20 a night, up from 13:14 last season, and is on the ice for 83% of Columbus's power-play chances, up from 37%. The result is 22 points in 21 games after 22 points in 76 last season, and a five-game point streak.

The role change is real, and so is a step forward in his own chances, up to 0.96 expected goals per 60 from 0.69. The finishing is the part to treat carefully: nine goals on 6.1 expected, shooting 18% after 6% last season. His 3.43 points per 60 sits well above our range of 1.68 to 2.45. Some regression is coming even if the breakout holds.

The doubt is in last season's record. Evolving-Hockey had Columbus creating 0.18 fewer expected goals per 60 with him on the ice in 2025-26, bottom 6% of forwards. This season the Blue Jackets are even with him at five-on-five, a real improvement. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 52% of his shots coming off the rush. Our numbers project 63 points.
headline: Kent Johnson's breakout is real, the shooting isn't
